narrative.overview:
The neighborhood is an RPG overworld. Every control is a real landmark drawn as a 16x16 sprite on a recolored map, and each landmark speaks its story fragment in a handheld dialogue box. That spoken fragment is what the walker carries in their head.

The world is one flat scheme in Sweetie 16: blue-grey ground, pale panel paper, deep ink, a single crimson action colour. Everything is hard-edged, with 0 radius and 2 dp rules stepped at the corners. Type is pixel faces only.

Green is rare on purpose: parks, woods, the park sprite and the found state. The memorable moment is the 4-step palette fade from ground to the run field when the walk begins.
keyCharacteristics: One Sweetie 16 scheme, no dark mode
Pixel boxes: 2 dp ink rules, stepped corners, double border for emphasis
Original 16x16 sprites in a shared 3/4 top-down view (18 landmark kinds)
Jersey 10 for speech, Press Start 2P for labels
Green only where it means nature or found
Run screen on a deep ink field with light text

rules.name: The Meaningful Green Rule
rules.body: Green marks only parks, woods, the park sprite and the found state. Everywhere else, colour follows what the element is.

rules.name: The One Action Colour Rule
rules.body: Crimson #B13E53 appears only on pressable primary actions (and the loading-bar fill); it flips to ink when pressed.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Jersey 10 speaks (story, body, titles); Press Start 2P labels (headings, buttons, numbers). Press Start 2P stays short and sparse because it is wide.

rules.name: The No-Soft-Edges Rule
rules.body: Zero radius, 2 dp rules, stepped corners; no blurred or offset shadows. Depth comes from outline, double borders and tone steps.

rules.name: The Integer Scale Rule
rules.body: Sprites and the mark render nearest-neighbour at integer multiples of their native grid.

rules.name: The One Cadence Rule
rules.body: Every typed fragment uses 70 ms per character, with or without speech; the advance pointer shows only when typing is done.

dos: Do use the one Sweetie 16 palette in a single scheme; the system light/dark setting is ignored.
Do build every box from PixelBox: 2 dp ink rule, 0 radius, corners notched by painting the colour behind, never rounded.
Do set the story and body text in Jersey 10 (26 sp body, 22 sp small, 30 sp title) and labels and numbers in Press Start 2P (12 sp label, 16 sp headline, 22 sp display).
Do render sprites as crisp rects at integer scales (16x16 at 2x, 3x or 6x) and the mark at integer multiples of 96x112.
Do keep green (#38B764, #A7F070) for parks, woods, the park sprite and the found state, and give every other element colours suited to what it is.
Do use the action colour (#B13E53) only on pressable primary actions, with #F4F4F4 text.
Do keep targets at 48 dp or more, sp text, and cap label scaling with maxFontSizeMultiplier where wide Press Start 2P would break layout.
Do collapse animation under reduced motion: the palette fade becomes one instant cut, and the blink and loading bar stop.
donts: Don't add radii, anti-aliased or blurred shadows, gradients or glass; depth is outline, double border and a dithered ground shadow inside the sprite.
Don't use pure black or white grounds, or orange-on-black.
Don't copy any existing game's sprites, creatures, fonts, badges, place names or UI text; every asset here is original or the user's own logo work.
Don't put green on elements that are not nature or the found state.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyph characters as icons; icons are pixel glyphs drawn in glyphs.ts.
Don't stretch or smooth the Loci mark, and don't draw it below scale 1 (the checkpoint holes fill in).
Don't use a system display face; all display and label text is pixel type.
Don't treat the recorded drift (7-line fragments scrolling at font scale 1.3, the small adaptive-icon mark, no mark in the setup header) as rules for new surfaces.
